_meta.source: NOVA food classification system — Monteiro CA et al., Public Health Nutrition, 2019
_meta.how_to_update: Add entries to the appropriate nova_X array. NOVA classifies FOODS, not individual additives. The ingredient-level mappings below are derived from the NOVA definitions: if an ingredient only exists via industrial processing (Group 4), or is a whole food (Group 1), etc.
_meta.important: NOVA was designed for classifying whole food products, not individual additives. These ingredient-level mappings are interpretive — the USDA FoodData Central database does NOT include NOVA scores per ingredient. When a NOVA score is unavailable for a searched ingredient, the UI should display 'NOVA classification not available for this ingredient' rather than guessing.

nova_1.label: Unprocessed or minimally processed foods
nova_1.definition: Parts of plants or animals with no or minimal processing (drying, grinding, pasteurization, fermentation, freezing). No added substances.

nova_2.label: Processed culinary ingredients
nova_2.definition: Substances extracted and purified from Group 1 foods via pressing, refining, grinding, or milling. Used in kitchens to prepare Group 1 foods.

nova_3.label: Processed foods
nova_3.definition: Foods made by adding Group 2 ingredients to Group 1 foods, using preservation methods (canning, bottling, fermentation). Typically 2-3 ingredients.

nova_4.label: Ultra-processed food and drink products
nova_4.definition: Industrial formulations of substances derived from foods, with little if any intact food. Contain additives whose purpose is to imitate sensory qualities of Group 1 foods or disguise undesirable qualities of the final product.
